assertions.assert: It is long-lived: each request is `bot.ability.classifying.input` `{id, segments}`. It hears the tone of the longest of the request's `segments` (the first of equals; a segment with no span counts as long enough) through the speech service's `classify` (`POST {base}/emotion?sample_rate=R`); the service's `bot.ability.classifying.output` is answered to its parent as `bot.ability.classifying.output` exactly `{id, label, scores, valence, confidence}` (mosfet.py's `voice.Affect`), and logs `listening.affect` `heard <label> <confidence>`.
A segment shorter than `min_segment_seconds` (0.3 s) is never sent; with no segment left, nothing is asked and it answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message}`, the message being what it logs.

A tone not heard (the service's `bot.ability.failed`, an answer that is not an affect, the service ending or unable to run, or no answer within `timeout_ms`, 3 s) answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message}` and logs `listening.affect` `failed: <why>`, the message (mosfet.py's classify answers None).
